papers.title: $w_0$ Is All You Need: Field-Level Matching of General Dark Energy Models to $w_0$CDM Simulations
papers.abstract: We show that clustering in general dynamical dark energy models $w(z)$ can be predicted with constant dark energy $w_0\text{CDM}$ models at the field level via spectral equivalence. The prescription of this method requires equating comoving distances to the last scattering surface between predictor and target models, which is equivalent to requiring equal recent background expansion history averages. Dark energy models with the same distance thus form approximate equivalence classes, with nearly identical matter fields. To test the precision of spectral equivalence beyond the CPL parametrization, we run $N$-body simulations with various dynamical dark energy models, including spline-based $w(z)$, all matched to a single $w_0\text{CDM}$ run. Our measurements show that the power spectra of all matched dark energies agree with the predictor within $0.2\%$ up to $k = 0.5\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ and within $0.6\%$ up to $k = 1\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$. We also compare the non-Gaussian information contained in the simulated fields. Bispectra differ by at most $0.26\%$ across all runs up to $k = 0.5\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ and $1.75\%$ up to $k = 1\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$, while wavelet scattering transform coefficients are all within $0.05\%$. The decorrelation, $1 - r^2$, between each matched field and the predictor stays below $0.006\%$ up to $k = 1\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$. We run a toy power spectrum analysis in the CPL parametrization demonstrating that a $w_0$-only emulator could produce the same posterior without any knowledge of the full $w_0w_a$ model. This matching prescription thus offers a new tool to constrain dynamical dark energy models with arbitrary equations of state at the field level, without running additional simulation suites.

papers.title: Bounds on entanglement fluctuations at holographic interfaces
papers.abstract: How small can entanglement fluctuations be at fixed entropy? For a class of holographic conformal interfaces supported by a scalar with a potential, we prove $c_\text{eff}\leq c_\text{cap}\leq c_\text{eff}^2/c_{LR}$, relating entropy, capacity, and energy transmission. The coupled gravitational response is a transport term minus a positive scalar contribution; the background Einstein equation bounds that subtraction. A long Janus throat allows unbounded capacity at a finite entropy coefficient while the scalar response remains gapped.

papers.title: A note on Holographic Renormalization for Polarized IKKT
papers.abstract: We construct a boundary counterterm for the on-shell action of type IIB supergravity solutions dual to vacua of the polarized IKKT matrix model. The construction is based on the variational principle, with off-shell fluctuations whose fall-off conditions are based on the asymptotic equations of motion. The renormalized on-shell action of the supersymmetric saddles reproduces the matrix- model result once we pass to the ensemble of fixed D1-brane charges, which we implement off-shell by dualizing the RR two-form potential.

papers.title: Pseudoscalar Yukawa Preheating via Effective Action Approach
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate helicity-dependent fermion production driven by a pseudoscalar Yukawa interaction within the one-loop effective action framework. By integrating out the fermionic fields and employing the Schwinger proper time representation, we derive an analytical expression for the fermion pair production probability near each zero crossing of the oscillating inflaton field. We further introduce a helicity transfer matrix to describe the evolution of fermionic modes through successive non-adiabatic production events. For an undamped inflaton background, the temporal symmetry around successive zero crossings leads to the cancellation of helicity-mixing contributions after an even number of events, preventing the accumulation of helicity asymmetry. We then extend the analysis to a damped oscillatory background, in which the decreasing inflaton amplitude breaks this temporal symmetry and modifies the transfer matrix at each crossing. The resulting non-commuting transfer matrices produce a persistent helical spectrum, as demonstrated by the probabilities as a function of momentum obtained after successive scattering events. A comparison with scalar Yukawa preheating further confirms the role of helicity mixing in generating the helical asymmetry induced by pseudoscalar mechanism. These results establish an effective action framework for studying helicity asymmetry during fermionic preheating and provide insight into the influence of the inflaton's dynamical evolution on particle production.

papers.title: Direct quantum simulation of compressible Navier-Stokes flow via finite homotopy linearisation
papers.abstract: We develop a direct quantum simulation algorithm for finite homotopy approximations to the non-isothermal compressible Navier-Stokes equations. A primitive-variable formulation gives polynomial residuals in the fields and their spatial and time derivatives, including density-weighted time derivatives. On a periodic grid, applying each spatial stencil uniformly to every factor in a shifted product preserves the dynamics of the finite homotopy hierarchy in an affine linearisation. Because each deformation equation depends only on lower homotopy orders, the lifted generator matrix is strictly block lower-triangular and hence nilpotent. The resulting finite-polynomial solution evaluates the final state directly without time-stepping error, while explicit short-time convergence conditions bound the homotopy truncation error on a fixed grid. In two-dimensional Taylor-Green flow, initial pressure balance removes the leading longitudinal acceleration and delays the onset of dilatational kinetic energy from quadratic to quartic in time. At Mach numbers 0.2 and 0.4, the fifth-order hierarchy reproduces viscous dissipation over a longer interval than pressure-dilatation at the same relative tolerance. We identify auxiliary variables representing the same evolving product, compile the finite-polynomial evolution into logical quantum circuits, and recover a signed velocity Fourier mode via Hadamard interference. Together, the Taylor-Green energy budgets quantify the accuracy windows of each homotopy order, while coarse-grid circuits verify the signed readout and measure gate counts. For higher-order evolution on finer grids, merging coincident stencil terms and combining block-encoded products along strictly increasing homotopy-order paths substantially reduce the predicted normalisation cost.

papers.title: Scattering amplitudes in AdS$_5\times$ S$^5$ from the pure spinor superstring
papers.abstract: We formulate a BRST-invariant prescription for the integration of zero modes in the pure spinor superstring on $AdS_5\times S^5$. The measure includes contributions absent in flat space and admits a description in terms of picture changing operators or a non-minimal regulator. The prescription is valid for genus-zero amplitudes with arbitrary multiplicity and external states and removes a central obstacle to amplitude computations in this background. We use it to perform the first direct worldsheet computation of two and three-point amplitudes of half-BPS supergravity states. The properly normalised three-point amplitudes exactly reproduce the results of planar ${\mathcal N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory.

papers.title: Using fixed $w$ to reproduce evolving $w_0$-$w_a$ dark energy at the field level
papers.abstract: Recent results from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) hint at dynamical dark energy, making the accurate modelling of such cosmologies increasingly important for future analyses. In this work, we show that because, when written in superconformal time $τ$, the $N$-body equations of motion depend on the background cosmology only through the expansion history $a(τ)$, matching $a(τ)$ allows us to map one cosmology onto another. As a first, observationally relevant, application of this new method, we match a Chevallier--Polarski--Linder (CPL) cosmology to a constant-$w$ cosmology with the closest $a(τ)$. This allows us to use a single fixed-$w$ simulation to reproduce the simulation predictions of the target CPL cosmology at the field level at redshifts $0\le z\le3$. We validate this matching with 100 pairs of CPL and fixed-$w$ \textsc{mg-glam} simulations, spanning $0.1\leΩ_{\rm m}\le0.5$, $-1.4\le w_0\le-0.5$ and $-1.8\le w_a\le-0.15$. For a DESI-like cosmology, the matter power spectra of the matched and target simulations agree to 0.24\% for $k\lesssim1\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ and 0.8\% up to $k\lesssim3\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ at $0\le z\le3$, and the density phases are reproduced with a stochasticity below 0.02\%. Displacements, velocities, momenta, redshift-space multipoles, bispectra and the halo and void abundances are similarly well predicted. For most models we consider, we achieve subpercent error in the power spectrum up to scales $k\lesssim1\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ at all redshifts, with density stochasticity below 0.03\% over the same scales. The method allows constant-$w$ simulations and field-level emulators to be used for CPL cosmologies, and generalises to any cosmology with no additional scale dependence.

papers.title: $μ$- and $q$-extension of special functions in quantum field theory
papers.abstract: Analytic calculations up to single-scale quantities in perturbative quantum field theory result into special numbers and functions, which are generalizations as iterative integrals over special alphabets. In this way one obtains polylogarithms, Nielsen integrals, the iterated integrals over linear denominator terms, cyclotomic letters, letters induced by quadratic forms, and square-root valued letters. The inverse Mellin transform relates special nested sums to these quantities, which are harmonic sums, generalized harmonic sums, nested sums implied by quadratic forms, cyclotomic harmonic sums, and nested sums containing central binomials. We construct the $μ$- and $q$-extensions of all these special functions. They are expected to occur in loop calculations within $μ$- and $q$-extended quantum field theories via modified (anti)commutation relations. The $μ$-extended special functions are quite different form the corresponding $q$-extended functions. While in the former case one observes class-preservation characterized by the polynomial $μ$-parameter, except for the case of root-valued letters. In the latter case new higher transcendental functions are obtained.

papers.title: Quantum coherence and entanglement of mixed states in relativistic settings
papers.abstract: States prepared in laboratory experiments are generally mixed because of imperfect preparation and residual coupling to the environment, whereas pure initial states represent an idealized limit. Motivated by this distinction, we investigate quantum entanglement and coherence in a pair of Unruh-DeWitt detectors initially prepared in a general two-qubit X state. One detector remains inertial and uncoupled, while the other undergoes uniform acceleration and interacts locally with a massless scalar field in the Minkowski vacuum. We obtain the reduced detector state within a perturbative treatment and evaluate its concurrence, $l_1$ norm of coherence, and relative entropy of coherence. For the initial-state families considered, the resulting expressions exhibit entanglement sudden death at finite acceleration, with larger initial entanglement associated with a higher threshold. Both coherence measures remain nonzero beyond this threshold and approach zero in the formal infinite-acceleration limit of these expressions. We also examine the dependence of these resources on the detector energy gap and interaction duration. The results distinguish the persistence of coherence from that of entanglement in the mixed-state detector model and identify initial mixedness as a relevant ingredient in relativistic quantum information.

papers.title: Where to Hide the Traps: Robust Placement in Verifiable Blind Quantum Computation
papers.abstract: Trap-based verification of blind quantum computation hides test qubits among the positions of a measurement pattern, and existing protocols choose the trap configuration without regard to the delegated computation. We model trap placement as a zero-sum game between a client, who chooses a trap distribution, and a server, who chooses where to apply a Pauli deviation, with a damage profile $w$ and a per-trap detection constant $c$. Since the client cannot know how damage from several positions combines, we solve the game for all monotone subadditive damage functions consistent with $w$ at once. In a single round, placing traps in proportion to $w$ guarantees soundness error $1-c/\|w\|_1$ and is optimal up to a factor $1+\max_iw_i$, while the optimistic solution can fail completely. Over $T$ test rounds, the error decays exponentially against a server that repeats the same deviation, but a general server can keep it at $Θ(\|w\|_1/(cT))$, and against such servers the damage-weighted placement is exactly optimal. Damage profiles follow from the flow of the pattern: for brickwork patterns with $m=4h+1$ columns, only $(2h+1)^2$ positions can affect a decision qubit, whatever the width. With $k$ traps per round, placing them on this set reduces the number of test rounds by the same factor as for a single trap; with unrestricted trap sets and flat damage we recover the known optimality of fractional coloring. Finally, trap statistics certify the aggregate damage with a number of rounds independent of the number of positions $N$, whereas locating the damage requires $Ω(Nε^{-2}\logδ^{-1})$ rounds.

papers.title: Constraining Dehnen-inspired dark matter halo with S2 star's orbit
papers.abstract: We use the orbit of S2 star around Sagittarius A* to constrain three black hole backgrounds motivated by Dehnen profiles with inner slopes $γ=0$, $1$, and $5/2$, which are characterized by the scale radius $r_s$ and density $ρ_s$ of the dark matter halo. An exact turning-point integral gives the pericenter advance at finite eccentricity, and an exterior expansion identifies the leading halo contributions. A fifteen-parameter Bayesian analysis combines astrometric and spectroscopic observations with the measured precession parameter, from which we obtain the marginalized $1σ$ upper limits $r_s/M<0.236$, $0.168$, and $0.030$, and $ρ_sM^2<0.536$, $0.578$, and $0.004$, respectively. The leading halo monopole in the first two metrics is degenerate with the central mass. At fixed dynamical mass, their leading radial profile correction produces retrograde precession. The $γ=5/2$ metric introduces an additional angular deficit contribution, which enhances the precession response and accounts for its smaller parameter limits.

papers.title: Quantifying the Impact of Galactic Dark Matter Halo Models on LZ Results
papers.abstract: Most dark matter direct-detection limits are reported under the assumption of an isotropic, Maxwellian Standard Halo Model. However, the Milky Way's stellar halo exhibits substantial radial anisotropy, while cosmological simulations predict scale-dependent anisotropy in the dark matter velocity distribution. We investigate how departures from isotropy affect the interpretation of LZ results in two complementary regimes: background-dominated elastic-scattering searches and the recently reported 248 keV nuclear-recoil candidate, which we study using a background-free single-event approximation. For elastic scattering, we use the self-consistent isotropic, Osipkov-Merritt, axisymmetric, and triaxial halo models of Belli et al. and translate the published limits through the ratio of predicted event counts, applying a common escape-speed truncation in the Galactic frame. At WIMP masses above approximately 40 GeV, the resulting limits lie within about $\pm 30\%$ of the isotropic reference. Below approximately 15 GeV, the model envelope broadens to as much as an order of magnitude, reflecting sensitivity to the high-velocity tail. For the 248 keV event, the accessible inelastic mass splitting is likewise controlled by this tail. Some anisotropic models extend the allowed kinematic region towards splittings at which solar-neutrino constraints on a Higgsino interpretation become ineffective, although kinematic accessibility alone does not establish viability at the fixed Higgsino cross section. These results show that halo-model dependence is modest at high WIMP masses but becomes essential near kinematic thresholds.

papers.title: Semiclassical Weyl laws and noncommutative geometry on open manifolds with conformally cusp metrics
papers.abstract: We establish semiclassical Weyl laws on open Riemannian manifolds with conformally cusp metrics of finite volume. These metrics need not be complete, and even when complete they do not have bounded geometry. Moreover, the potentials are bounded, the discreteness of the spectrum being a consequence of the geometry rather than of a confining potential. Therefore, our results lie beyond the scope of recent semiclassical Weyl laws of Dai--Yan and Braverman. The semiclassical Weyl laws are established for fractional Schrödinger operators associated with Dirac operators, magnetic Laplacians, and Hodge Laplacians, under conditions of Moroianu and Golénia--Moroianu which ensure that these operators have discrete spectra. We also obtain extensions of Connes' integration formula for the same operators. In addition, we deal with a class of conformally cusp metrics of infinite volume, in which case the semiclassical Weyl laws and the integration formulas only involve the values at infinity. The results are obtained by applying the abstract semiclassical Weyl laws and integration formulas for spectral triples established in a previous paper.

papers.title: Exact stress-tensor fluctuations from conformal symmetry and black hole radiation
papers.abstract: Semiclassical gravity is sourced by the expectation value of the stress tensor, and it is reliable only if the fluctuations around this value are small. In two dimensions, conformal symmetry captures the essential physics of Hawking radiation in its s-wave sector and determines the mean value exactly, for any background and any quantum state. We show that it also determines the local fluctuations of the null components $T_{\pm\pm}$. The square of the stress tensor is defined by the operator product expansion, up to a multiple $α$ of $\partial_\pm^2T_{\pm\pm}$ that labels point-splitting prescriptions. Its transformation law under the conformal map to locally inertial coordinates gives the variance in closed form. The relative fluctuation scales as $1/c$, with $c$ the central charge. For the Schwarzschild black hole it is $22/5c$ for the Hawking flux at infinity, that of flat-space thermal radiation. At the horizon it is $-44α/3c$ for the outgoing flux and $(238+720α)/5c$ for the ingoing flux that drives the backreaction. Both reduce to $22/5c$ for $α=-3/10$, which corresponds to the Möbius-covariant prescription. For large $c$ these results support the semiclassical approximation.

papers.title: Quasinormal Modes and Excitation Factors of a Parity-Symmetric Beyond-Horndeski Black Hole
papers.abstract: We study scalar, electromagnetic, and Dirac perturbations of an asymptotically flat black hole in parity-symmetric beyond-Horndeski gravity. The quasinormal spectrum is computed with very-high-order WKB expansions and Padé resummation, with Cesàro means used to diagnose internal convergence. The dominant modes are independently tested by time-domain evolution with Prony extraction and by Chebyshev pseudospectral collocation; the latter also provides systematic frequency scans in both the metric-scale and physical ADM-mass normalizations. Excitation factors are obtained separately from Green-function residues by complex-contour integration. In the fixed metric-scale normalization, approaching Schwarzschild generally increases both the oscillation frequency and damping rate, whereas stronger deformation shifts the modes toward lower frequencies and weaker damping. In ADM-mass units, the mildly deformed solutions remain close to Schwarzschild, while the most deformed sector becomes enhanced and nonmonotonic because the asymptotic mass itself varies strongly. The independent methods agree very well, however the sixth-order WKB approximation used in [G. Antoniou, T. D. Pappas, P. Kanti, Phys. Rev. D 112, 084013 (2025)] is insufficient in certain regions of the parameter space: the fundamental-mode discrepancy reaches nine percent in the damping rate and the first-overtone discrepancy can be of order unity. The Schwarzschild excitation factors are recovered. In the strongly deformed regime, their magnitudes can differ from the Schwarzschild values by more than two orders of magnitude in the asymptotic tortoise-coordinate convention. We show that this large effect is predominantly due to the deformation-dependent displacement of the potential barrier in the tortoise coordinate: when its maximum is used as the origin, the excitation factors exhibit much more modest deviations.

papers.title: Unruh-like effects and correlation harvesting between particle detectors in uniform motion in (2+1)-dimensional Minkowski spacetime
papers.abstract: We study Gaussian-switched Unruh-DeWitt detectors coupled to a massless scalar field in the (2+1)-dimensional Minkowski vacuum and following four classes of uniformly accelerated trajectories: linear, catenary, cusped, and circular motion. We first determine how the single-detector transition probability and effective temperature depend on acceleration and the torsion-to-acceleration ratio $\bar{b}$, whose continuous variation connects these four trajectory classes. We find that both quantities generally increase with acceleration, while their dependence on $\bar{b}$ can become nonmonotonic depending on the energy gap. We also examine a correlation-harvesting protocol by two detectors following horizontally displaced copies of the same trajectory. Increasing acceleration or separation generally suppresses the harvested concurrence and quantum mutual information, but the extent of suppression at fixed acceleration depends strongly on the trajectory class. For each of the four trajectory classes, we identify regimes of genuine entanglement harvesting in which vacuum correlations alone suffice to entangle the detectors, while the communication contribution alone cannot overcome local noise.

papers.title: A Frequency-Learning Interpolation-Based Coordinate Descent Method to Optimize Parameterized Quantum Circuits on Quantum Hardware
papers.abstract: Structure-aware optimizers have been the focus of recent study for the optimization of parameters in variational quantum circuits. Many of these optimizers follow a coordinate-based paradigm, making single parameter updates by using classical approximations to the cost function generated from quantum sampling. However, the performance of structure-aware optimizers on real quantum hardware at large system size has yet to be demonstrated. Recently, Interpolation-based Coordinate Descent (ICD) has been proposed to unify many of these optimizers into one framework. ICD requires a preset frequency set for interpolation, which can be theoretically derived, but for which the cost function is generally sparse over and may require manual tuning. To address these issues, we propose Frequency-learning Interpolation-based Coordinate Descent (FLICD) to adaptively learn frequencies online, allowing easier scaling up to larger systems. We demonstrate that our algorithm is more accurate than an existing zeroth-order method COBYLA and requires fewer quantum resources than ICD on simulator. Using IBM quantum hardware, we execute FLICD on systems up to 100 qubits and observe robust performance with an increasing number of layers.

papers.title: Scale-dependent Dark Matter in a Multi-component Cosmological Framework: Distinct Components Governing Galactic and Cosmological Dynamics
papers.abstract: In this work we generalize the concept of scale-dependent equation of state dark matter from galactic to cosmological scales. At galactic scales, the scale-dependent equation of state which successfully describes dark matter dominated galaxies has a nearly isothermal equation of state of the form $P(r)=K(r)ρ(r)$, where the entropy function $K(r)$ is radius dependent and slowly varying with the galactic radius. Using appropriate theoretical arguments, the successful galactic scale dark matter model is generalized to have a universal equation of state of the form $\langle P(χ)\rangle =\langle ρ(χ)\rangle \langle σ_{DM}^2\rangle$, where $χ$ is the scale of the system under study and it can describe cosmological or galactic scales and $σ_{DM}$ is the characteristic velocity dispersion of dark matter at the relevant scales. This results to the entropy function behaving universally as $K(χ)=\langle σ_{DM}^2\rangle$. We investigate the cosmological implications of scale-dependent equation of state dark matter, and we conclude that this scale-dependent equation of state dark matter cannot be the sole component of dark matter in the Universe. Also the second aim of this work is to provide a sufficient explanation for the question why $K_0$ changes for each galaxy, where $K_0$ is the value of $K(r)$ at intermediate and large radii from the core of the galaxy. Furthermore, we introduce the concept of having distinct dark matter components which cluster differently, and thus controlling differently the dynamics of the Universe at various scales. Scale-dependent equation of state dark matter can control the galactic scales, while another component can dominate at cosmological scales and thus control the Universe at cosmological scales.

papers.title: Anti-de Sitter charges and maximal Cauchy hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We construct conserved charges of asymptotic symmetries for negative-cosmological-constant vacuum spacetimes from the Neumann data for the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints on maximal conformally-compact Cauchy hypersurfaces. This gives a general and canonical initial value treatment of charges for vacuum spacetimes with timelike conformal boundary.

papers.title: Finite-Time Singularities of the $L_β$-Gradient Flow in a Kähler Surface
papers.abstract: We study finite-time singularities of the $L_β$-gradient flow of closed symplectic surfaces in a compact Kähler surface, with $β> 0$ fixed. We derive the evolution equation for the second fundamental form and obtain a lower bound on the blow-up rate of its maximum squared norm. Combining this bound with a local curvature propagation estimate and the weighted monotonicity formula, we rule out Type I singularities.

papers.title: Inner derivations and automorphism groups of vertex operator algebras
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a simple, rational, $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra of CFT type. We prove that the zero mode map $V_1\to\operatorname{Der}(V)$, $h\mapsto h_0$, is an isomorphism of Lie algebras. We prove surjectivity using traces on finite sums of weight spaces and Li's module construction, and injectivity using the vacuum character of Zhu's algebra. It follows that $\operatorname{Inn}(V)$ is the identity component of $\operatorname{Aut}(V)$ and has finite index in $\operatorname{Aut}(V)$. Moreover, $\operatorname{dim}\operatorname{Aut}(V)=\dim V_1$, so $\operatorname{Aut}(V)$ is finite if and only if $V_1=0$.

papers.title: Massive Particles in Carrollian Holography
papers.abstract: Understanding how massive particles are encoded in boundary operators is a central problem in Carrollian holography. We construct a three-dimensional Carrollian description of a massive scalar in four-dimensional flat spacetime, together with an explicit bulk-to-boundary integral transform. In this construction, nonzero mass requires infinitely many linearly independent primary states, while the absence of bulk spin imposes relations among their descendants. We show that these relations are equivalent to null-state decoupling and give a local constraint on the boundary fields. The integral transform preserves the full Poincaré symmetry and maps bulk scalar data to fields satisfying this constraint. We also obtain two- and three-point functions and the associated formal operator product expansion coefficients. The integral transform evaluates bulk data at complex momenta, making analytic continuation essential in Lorentzian signature. This construction provides a concrete starting point for relating massive scattering amplitudes to Carrollian correlators and for reconstructing bulk fields from boundary data.

papers.title: Orthosymplectic $K$-matrices in small dimensions
papers.abstract: Using elementary methods, we describe coideal subalgebras of quantum orthosymplectic algebras of small dimensions, classify the corresponding $K$-matrices and find explicitly the centralizers of these subalgebras in the vector representation. The main attention is paid to generators with a Cartan term. For them, at generic values of the parameters, we find the centralizers and all $K$-matrices and describe the decomposition of the vector representation over the coideal subalgebra. We find all special values of the parameters of two types and, at a generic point of each set of special values, describe the decomposition of the vector representation and all $K$-matrices. At special values of the first type the dimension of the centralizer grows. One hypersurface of such values is related to Cartan terms, and on it one of the generators is given by the same formula as in the quantum electrical algebra. At special values of the second type the dimension of the centralizer is the same, but nonzero nilpotent elements appear in it. The $K$-matrices on the sets of special values of the second type are obtained from those already found by substituting the condition, and there are no others. We describe the classical limit, including the limit of special values. We formulate an observation relating the admissibility of a Cartan term to the first homology of the classical subalgebra.

papers.title: Numerical Integration of Geodesic Motion in Non-Schwarzschild Spacetimes
papers.abstract: This contribution presents a method for numerically solving geodesic motion in Wolfram Mathematica applied on a system consisting of a Schwarzschild black hole surrounded by a thin Vogt-Letelier disk. While geodesic motion in the Schwarzschild spacetime is fully integrable due to its high degree of symmetry, the addition of a disk breaks the spherical symmetry and leads to a weak-integrable dynamical system. Particular attention is paid to the treatment of particle trajectories near the thin disk, where discontinuities in the derivatives of the metric may affect numerical stability and the conservation of integrals of motion. Several numerical treatments of disk crossings were implemented, arriving to a method based on the re-normalization of the four-velocity. The phase-space of the system is investigated using Poincaré sections and rotation number spectra.

papers.title: The chiral $M^{3,2}$ theory: partition functions beyond large-$N$ and quantum holography
papers.abstract: We identify families of Bethe vacua in the chiral $M^{3,2}$ theory whose individual free energies grow as $N^{3/2}$. High-precision data support closed forms for their all-order perturbative $1/N$ expansions. At a distinguished mixed Chern--Simons coupling, the baryonic magnetic flux distinguishes members of this family of vacua. We also study the three-sphere partition function numerically in the 't Hooft limit and Cardy limit, and propose an all-order Airy formula. The four-derivative and one-loop corrections are precision tests of holography.

papers.title: Superintegrable Systems and the Tractor Connection
papers.abstract: Quadratic constants of motion for natural pseudo-Riemannian Hamiltonians with potential correspond to conformal Killing tensors admitting multiple Killing scales. Taking this correspondence further, we develop a dimension-independent ($n\ge 3$) framework for studying second-order superintegrable systems using conformal tractor calculus, and invariant BGG prolongation of the rank two conformal Killing equation. We apply this framework to classify second-order maximally superintegrable systems within certain natural families of Hamiltonians generated by pairs of conformally related Einstein metrics in arbitrary dimensions. We recover the second-order analogue of Bertrand's theorem as a special case.

papers.title: Radial stability of nonlinearly scalarized black holes in Einstein-phantom scalar-Gauss-Bonnet theory
papers.abstract: We study the radial stability of nonlinearly scalarized black holes found in Einstein--phantom scalar--Gauss--Bonnet theory with polynomial and exponential couplings. Two branches of lower and primary are found for phantom scalarized black holes. The coupled scalar--metric perturbations reduce to a Schrödinger-type equation, after eliminating redundant metric perturbations. The lower branch including the pure quartic solutions has one growing mode, while positive zero-energy solutions for the primary branch could establish stability through the $S$-deformation method. Stable primary solutions are found for the exponential coupling. Also, we explore the connection between radial stability and thermodynamic analysis for two branches. Furthermore, we show that canonical scalarized black holes obtained from Einstein--scalar--Gauss--Bonnet theory with polynomial coupling reveals unstable lower and stable primary branches.

papers.title: Subquantum Pilot-Wave System Theory: Structural and Amplitude Nonequilibrium under Source Fields
papers.abstract: A source in the Schrodinger equation changes the norm of the guiding wave, apparently conflicting with the conservation of probability. In source-extended de Broglie-Bohm dynamics the conflict disappears: probability is carried by the particle ensemble, while the wavefunction guides its motion. The difficulty is then different. What does quantum equilibrium mean when the particle distribution remains normalized but the guiding density does not? We show that the departure has two independent components: a structural one, measured by the Kullback--Leibler divergence between the particle distribution and the normalized guiding density, and an amplitude one, measured by the Born weight. The Born rule holds precisely when both are equilibrated. Their evolution is governed by the complex source-to-wavefunction ratio; scale covariance further distinguishes an independently prescribed source, against which the amplitude of the wave matters, from state-dependent generators for which rescaling remains a symmetry. We develop a source-aware analytical--computational method, combining exact or semi-analytical guiding fields with Bohmian trajectory transport, ensemble quadrature and independent numerical checks. Free-space impulses expose the limits of global diagnostics and an exact jump rule; a driven ring has constant Born weight but either periodic or secular structural departure; oscillators show both source-generated structural change and amplitude-only evolution, including a finite-horizon weak-drive plateau far below its frozen-particle value; and a coupled two-body model exhibits nonlocal guidance and evolving particle entanglement. The source-free, initially equilibrated sector recovers standard quantum mechanics.

papers.title: Scalar dynamics in a subclass Ia mimetic DHOST bounce
papers.abstract: We study scalar perturbations in a quadratic subclass Ia degenerate higher-order scalar-tensor (DHOST) realization of a nonsingular bouncing cosmology previously analyzed in higher-derivative mimetic gravity. After a constant rescaling of the scalar potential, the subclass Ia model reproduces the same scale-factor history as the original model, although the associated mimetic Lagrange multiplier generally differs. For the comparison with the original mimetic model, we focus on the branch $0<γ<2/3$, for which the scalar sound speed of the original model is positive. We perform an ADM and Hamiltonian reduction of the scalar sector and show that, imposing the mimetic and momentum constraints, the reduced canonical scalar mode contains no spatial-gradient contribution. The physical scalar sound speed therefore vanishes, $c_s^2=0$, in agreement with the known vacuum behavior of the \(α_L=0\) mimetic-DHOST sector. On the matched bouncing background, the resulting effective frequency squared is independent of the comoving wavenumber and approaches zero from below in the remote contracting phase. Consequently, the asymptotic oscillatory regime used in the previous mimetic model to impose positive-frequency initial conditions is absent. Although canonical normalization can still be imposed through the Wronskian condition, it does not select the initial state uniquely. Without an additional state prescription, the asymptotic dynamics therefore does not uniquely determine the primordial scalar spectrum.

papers.title: Similarity preserving noncommutative maps
papers.abstract: In this note we study similarity preserving automorphisms of noncommutative (NC for short) balls. We show that every similarity preserving NC automorphism is, in fact, given by a similarity with an NC invertible function. As an application, we show that the group of automorphisms of the free semigroup algebra is generated by unitarily implemented and inner automorphisms.

papers.title: Verification and Evaluation of A Comprehensive Quantum Simulation Compiler
papers.abstract: Hamiltonian simulation is a central application of quantum computing, yet most existing compilers offer no machine-checked guarantee that the circuits they produce approximate the intended evolution. The previous QBlue compiler verifies a Hamiltonian simulation compiler containing only Trotter-based algorithms. It takes a Hamiltonian written over Pauli strings, a simulation time, and an error bound, and produces a circuit or analog schedule that is proven, in the Rocq proof assistant, to approximate the ideal time evolution within that bound and proves a single end-to-end error bound that composes the errors of the individual stages; the compiler uses it to select, by resource estimation, the cheapest algorithm that meets the user's bound. This paper advances the verification efforts with two further steps. First, we extend QBlue to $\textsf{QBlue}_{\texttt{BE}}$ by verifying another important compilation method for Hamiltonian simulation: block-encoding-based (BE-based) algorithms. Second, we empirically evaluate 279 Hamiltonian simulation programs against the state-of-the-art BE-based compiler, PennyLane. For many programs, our compiler shows a $94\%$ gate reduction compared to PennyLane. Additionally, we also discover issues and bugs in PennyLane. We also compare Trotter- and BE-based algorithms, providing a practical comparison for the long-standing debate over which algorithms perform better. Our results surprisingly show that Trotter-based algorithms may gain a practical advantage, even though BE algorithms have a theoretical advantage.

papers.title: Online Scheduling for Entanglement Distillation: Learning When to Wait
papers.abstract: Entanglement distillation probabilistically increases the fidelity of entangled pairs at the cost of reducing their number. The outcome of each distillation operation takes time to communicate, during which the entangled pairs decohere while idle in their memories. This raises a dilemma: wait for the outcome before proceeding, or continue optimistically at the risk of needlessly consuming further pairs. We study online distillation scheduling, in which distillation trees are constructed dynamically to maximize the throughput of pairs that meet a required fidelity. A policy decides which pairs to distill together and, for each operation, whether to wait for its outcome. We derive an upper bound on the throughput of every scheduling policy and, by formulating the problem as a Markov decision process, train, with reinforcement learning, a policy that applies to any number of memories. Compared with two baselines that always or never wait, the learned policy delivers as many pairs of the required fidelity as the better one when one of these two extremes is the best choice, and more otherwise.

papers.title: Incompressible quantum information
papers.abstract: For a small classical system correlated with a large one, it is always possible to compress the large system down to a size only dependent on the size of the smaller one, while preserving all correlations up to a given controllable error. Here, we show that such a statement does not hold at all when the large system is quantum mechanical. More precisely, we show that there are bipartite states such that any compression of the large system, by a non-trivial relative factor, will necessarily lead to the destruction of a significant amount of correlation, measured in mutual information. Our results therefore identify a limitation of information-bottleneck approaches to quantum machine learning, showing that a small system specifying the relevant features contained in a large quantum data set does not guarantee a compact encoding of the latter that preserves the relevant correlations.

papers.title: Dual Horizon-MAD: A New Mode of Binary Black Hole Magnetically Arrested Accretion with Saturated Horizon Magnetic Fluxes and Intermittent Minidisks
papers.abstract: Reliable first-principles predictions of multimessenger signals from inspiralling supermassive binary black holes (SMBBHs) require magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations in full general relativity (GR) that resolve the accretion flow down to the black hole horizons. However, performing such simulations long enough to relax the magnetohydrodynamics near the BBHs is computationally challenging and a source of uncertainty in modeling efforts. In this work, we present the longest MHD simulation of circumbinary disk (CBD) accretion onto a SMBBH in full GR. The equal-mass, quasicircular, nonspining BBH starts at an initial separation of $d/M=30$ and evolves over $\sim56$ orbits ($t \simeq 52,000 \, GM/c^3$), relaxing the magnetic field dynamics within the CBD cavity. After $\sim 23$ orbits and persistent magnetically arrested minidisks, the accretion enters a new magnetically arrested mode which we call dual horizon-MAD (DH-MAD). In DH-MAD, the dimensionless horizon magnetic fluxes remain saturated at $φ_{BH}\sim 20$ driving magnetic flux eruptions from the vicinity of the BH horizons, and the vertical magnetic flux in the cavity saturates, but no flux eruptions occur at the cavity-CBD boundary. During this DH-MAD phase, there is also a shift in the total mass accretion rate variability, which exhibits a periodicity of $f\sim 1.8 f_{\rm orb}$, while the accretion rate modulation on the individual black holes occurs almost at the orbital period, $f\sim 0.9 f_{\rm orb}$. $φ_{BH}$ also exhibits a robust periodicity at $f\sim 0.4 f_{\rm orb}$, suggesting that quasiperiodic nonthermal emission from magnetic reconnection near the horizons could be a smoking gun electromagnetic counterpart to inspiraling SMBBHs. Finally, minidisks around the BHs become intermittent in the DH-MAD phase, even at a separation of $d/M = 24$, likely due to the large plasma magnetization in the optically thin cavity.

papers.title: Higgs-portal dark matter beyond kinetic equilibrium
papers.abstract: We revisit the scalar, vector, and fermion Higgs-portal dark matter models in the resonant regime without assuming kinetic equilibrium during the freeze-out. We compute the relic abundance by solving the full momentum-dependent Boltzmann equation and compare the results with the standard momentum-averaged treatment. We find that the standard treatment significantly underestimates the relic abundance below the resonance, apart from the fermionic case with a purely scalar portal coupling where the difference is negligible. The deviation from the standard treatment is largest for fermionic models with pseudoscalar interactions, corresponding to factor of 10 in terms of the coupling that reproduces the correct relic abundance. For the scalar and vector cases the corresponding difference is up to a factor of 2. We confront the resulting parameter space with the latest constraints from direct and indirect detection, as well as collider experiments. We find the full momentum-dependent results systematically strengthen the direct detection constraints.

papers.title: Scotogenic dark matter from gauged $L_μ+L_τ$
papers.abstract: In this work, we introduce the first scotogenic model based on a gauged $L_μ + L_τ$ symmetry whose spontaneous breaking by two units leaves a remnant matter parity $M_P$. The resulting light active neutrinos are of Majorana nature and the lightest electrically neutral state mediating the scotogenic loop is stabilized by $M_P$ and can be identified as a weakly interacting massive particle dark matter candidate. We analyze the phenomenology of a predominantly singlet-like CP-even scalar dark matter candidate and the representative regions of parameter space compatible with the observed thermal relic abundance. The $Z'$ boson is compatible with a broad range of parameters relevant for dark matter. In particular, electroweak precision constraints do not lead to significant tensions for kinetic mixing values up to $ε\sim 10^{-2}$. We discuss the implications of existing searches for leptophilic gauge bosons and the conditions under which visible and invisible collider signatures become relevant.

papers.title: WIMPs as FIMPs: the Inert Doublet Model and low-temperature reheating
papers.abstract: Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs) are conventionally assumed to acquire their dark matter relic abundance through thermal freeze-out. However, this association relies on assumptions concerning the thermal history of the early Universe. We revisit the Inert Doublet Model (IDM), a representative WIMP framework in which dark matter interacts with the Standard Model through electroweak gauge interactions, even when its Higgs-portal coupling vanishes. We demonstrate that sufficiently low reheating temperatures can prevent chemical equilibrium, allowing a genuine WIMP to acquire its relic abundance through freeze-in rather than freeze-out. Considering both instantaneous and finite-duration reheating, we identify different production histories, including freeze-out during radiation domination, freeze-out during reheating, and freeze-in with potentially significant annihilation backreactions. These scenarios open regions of the IDM parameter space that would otherwise be excluded by dark matter overabundance. Our results demonstrate that WIMPs can behave as FIMPs, depending on the thermal history of the Universe.

papers.title: On the distribution function for cross-correlation estimators in cosmology and beyond
papers.abstract: The ubiquitous Gaussian distribution, $e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2π}$, has mean of zero and variance of 1. It is well known that the estimator $\widehat{x^2} = N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N x_i^2$ for the variance obtained from $N$ samples $x_i$ is drawn from a $χ_n^2$ distribution, a result used often to assess the implications of data for a model. One often also needs to measure the covariance, or cross-correlation, of two different variables $x$ and $y$. If the distributions for $x$ and $y$ are both gaussian but independent of each other, the estimator $N^{-1}\sum_i x_i y_i$ for the cross-correlation is distributed about its expectation value (zero) with variance unity. The distribution function for this estimator may also be required to interpret data, for example in the measurement of cosmological cross-correlations. This distribution---the cross-correlation analog of the $χ_n^2$ distribution---appears in the literature, but it has not been widely internalized by many in the field. We therefore here present two pedagogical derivations of this distribution and discuss some of its properties. We discuss in particular the connection to cosmological observables, but note several other areas of physics where these results may apply.

papers.title: Revealing Dark Matter in the Dark-Electron Rate of Xenon Detectors
papers.abstract: There is high interest in improving experimental sensitivity to sub-GeV dark matter (DM) that scatters with electrons, as compelling theoretical models seem within reach. At the lowest DM masses, most of the expected signal lies in the single-electron regime, but so do large backgrounds. Xenon experiments therefore either do not yet search there at all or, as in XENONnT, apply cuts so severe that only $\sim$$10^{-4}$ of the exposure is retained, with sensitivity set by the criterion $S \lesssim B$, where those are the signal and background counts. We advocate that xenon detectors instead utilize most of their dark-electron rate (i.e., the total raw electron hit rate) and perform an annual-modulation search, for which the sensitivity scales as $S \lesssim \sqrt{B}$. Modern DAQs already record this rate, continuously in triggerless systems such as the XENONnT and PandaX-4T DAQs, and within trigger windows in LZ, so no new hardware is required. Using measured dark-electron rates, we estimate the sensitivity of XENONnT, LZ, PandaX-4T, PandaX-xT, and XLZD. We find that dramatic gains in sensitivity are possible, motivating new analyses of present and future xenon data.

papers.title: Wormholes do not contribute to supersymmetric partition functions
papers.abstract: We show that wormholes connecting multiple asymptotic boundaries always spontaneously break at least some of the symmetries preserved by their boundary conditions. Their configurations then form nontrivial orbits of the broken symmetry, and for the case of a fermionic symmetry, the contribution of each orbit vanishes. We conclude that wormholes do not contribute to moments of supersymmetric partition functions. This extends results on supersymmetric indices by Iliesiu, Kologlu, and Turiaci. We emphasize that supersymmetric partition functions can still have a nonzero ensemble variance. In SYK-like examples that we analyze, this arises due to the contribution of ``non-geometric wormhole'' configurations that preserve all continuous symmetries.

papers.title: Level repulsion and the quantum viscosity of near-extremal black branes
papers.abstract: Below the gap scale of the AdS$_2$ throat, quantum fluctuations make the shear viscosity of near-extremal black branes grow as $(CT)^{-1/2}$ in the disk approximation of JT gravity, and the one-loop $η/s$ diverges. To cure this divergence, we include the non-perturbative completion of JT gravity as a matrix integral. The Kubo formula then probes universal features of level correlations. At finite extremal entropy $S_0$, level repulsion makes the DC viscosity vanish. A finite, universal viscosity survives in a double-scaling limit in which the probe frequency $ω$ is held in a fixed ratio to the level-spacing scale $ω_{\rm sp}\equiv e^{-S_0}/C$. At fixed $ω$, with $ω_{\rm sp}\llω\ll e^{S_0/3}ω_{\rm sp}$ the Schwarzian growth then saturates at $η_{\max}\simeq0.174\,(ω/ω_{\rm sp})\,η_{sc}$, where $η_{sc}$ is the semiclassical viscosity, and the viscosity decreases at lower temperatures. At the extremely low temperature scale $CT\sim e^{-2S_0/3}$ the genus expansion and the one-loop entropy computations completely break down. There we start probing the edge of the spectrum and the problem reduces exactly to the Airy kernel. We find that the ratio of the quenched averages of $η$ and $s$ is finite and positive at every non-zero temperature. We compare our results with explicit completions defined by the string equation, in which the spectrum is bounded from below. The bulk results are the same in these completions and the quenched edge results change only by a few per cent, while the annealed quantities depend on the non-perturbative completion at order one.

papers.title: Ohmic warm inflation
papers.abstract: We show that Warm Little Inflation is anomalous, lacks a suitable inflaton potential, and cannot sustain the thermal bath, as the quasi-static approximation over-estimated the dissipated power. To address these issues, we propose a new friction mechanism and new anomaly-free models based on one fermion charged under a U(1) gauge group in one extra dimension. The four-dimensional lattice version is a ring of $N$ U(1) groups with one fermion at each site, reducing to an anomaly-free version of the warm little inflaton model for $N=2$. The inflaton is a Wilson line, protected for $N\ge5$. Large $N$ allows a suitable monodromy inflaton potential. In the continuum limit, $N\to\infty$, the inflaton velocity becomes a five-dimensional electric field and friction becomes Ohmic dissipation, which seems able to sustain warm inflation compatibly with observations.

papers.title: Optimised 8th-Order Trotter-Suzuki Schemes for Quantum Simulation
papers.abstract: Simulating quantum dynamics in many-body systems is one of the most promising applications of quantum computers. Product formulas are a natural choice for this task, since they map directly onto quantum gates, and increasing their order $n$ could lead to reduced gate depths, provided the parameters are chosen efficiently. So far, schemes beyond $6^{\textrm{th}}$ order have only been built as compositions of second-order schemes, while more general product formulas are known only up to $6^{\textrm{th}}$ order. In this work, we extend our optimisation framework to order $n = 8$, and find both more efficient compositions and the first $8^{\textrm{th}}$ order general schemes. Our formulas improve on the theoretical efficiency of the state-of-the-art schemes by Morales et al and we recommend two schemes explicitly. In simulations of the Heisenberg XZ chain one of our recommended schemes always outperforms those by Morales et al, though it is not always the same scheme that performs best. More generally, we observe that for Hamiltonians split into many non-commuting operators the uniformity of a Trotter decomposition becomes the main indicator of a scheme's performance. To assess the schemes' use on quantum hardware, we simulate noisy circuits with our new Qiskit plugin qiskit-omelyan. At current noise levels, the Leapfrog scheme remains the best choice, but as noise rates decrease toward fault tolerance, our recommended schemes become competitive.

papers.title: World Models for Learning Quantum Many-Body Dynamics
papers.abstract: We propose using world models for learning Hamiltonians from measured dynamics of a quantum computer or simulator. Implicitly, the parameters of a Hamiltonian are encoded in how the measured few-body observables evolve. By using a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) to perform prediction in latent space, we show that the device Hamiltonian can be efficiently inferred from noisy measurements. We train a spatiotemporal encoder and predictor with approximately $2.7$ million trainable weights using a single objective, to predict the representation of the next window of measurements from the previous one. The network is thereby driven to retain the reproducible dynamics and discard shot noise. We recover the field and coupling maps of a two-dimensional Ising lattice in real and imaginary time, and the disorder map of a one-dimensional Heisenberg chain of $100$ sites. In every settings the encoder achieves lower error than a masked autoencoder and than the same encoder left untrained. It also outperforms the same regression head applied directly to time-averaged observables, by factors of $4.4$ to $30$. We establish latent prediction as a practical self-supervised objective for learning from measurements of quantum dynamics.

papers.title: Brane Tilings and Polygons with Two Interior Points
papers.abstract: We fully classify the brane tilings and the 4d N=1 supersymmetric quiver gauge theories corresponding to toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds whose toric diagrams are convex lattice polygons with two interior lattice points. There are 45 such polygons up to GL(2,Z) transformations and lattice translations: 5 triangles, 19 quadrilaterals, 16 pentagons and 5 hexagons. We identify all 323 toric phases corresponding to these toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds. For every toric phase, we present the brane tiling with its quiver and superpotential, the perfect matching matrix and the F- and D-term charge matrices. For each brane tiling, we study the mesonic moduli space of the corresponding abelian 4d N=1 theory through its Hilbert series and plethystic logarithm, and identify its generators and their leading relations. We also identify the mesonic global symmetry for each brane tiling and determine the superconformal U(1)R charges.

papers.title: Sampling non-abelian lattice gauge theories with diffusion models
papers.abstract: We present gauge-equivariant diffusion models as samplers for lattice gauge theories (LGTs). Using lattice gauge-equivariant convolutional neural networks (L-CNNs) and the Metropolis-adjusted annealed Langevin algorithm (MAALA), we are able to accurately sample two-dimensional U(2) field configurations and show first promising results for four-dimensional SU(3). Our two-dimensional models extrapolate remarkably well to larger inverse couplings than originally trained on. We confirm this by comparing observables to analytically known values and to hybrid Monte Carlo results.

papers.title: Autonomous quantum machine learning via Riemannian gradient-based optimization
papers.abstract: Quantum machine learning models typically rely on repeated quantum measurements and classical optimization during training, making the quantum-to-classical information-extraction process a fundamental bottleneck for scalability. We propose a framework for autonomous self-training quantum machine learning, based on Riemannian gradient optimization, in which the optimization proceeds entirely within the quantum domain without requiring quantum measurements or classical feedback. We derive the Riemannian gradient update rules for a broad class of learning tasks and identify sufficient conditions under which the resulting training dynamics can be realized fully autonomously. Within this regime, we establish an exponential convergence guarantee, in the training iterations, for sufficiently small step sizes, and further analyze the training cost in terms of the growth of the circuit depth. Importantly, we further show that the trained model can automatically discover symmetries hidden in the training data without $\textit{a priori}$ specification. For the canonical examples of quantum phase classification and unitary learning with a hidden symmetry, our numerical study indicates that learning can be achieved at low circuit depths with only a few distinct training examples. Our results thus establish autonomous quantum machine learning as a promising paradigm that removes the classical optimization loop while retaining strong theoretical guarantees and practical performances.

papers.title: Cosmic Censorship in the Landscape of SUSY-Broken AdS Vacua
papers.abstract: We investigate signatures of weak cosmic censorship in non-supersymmetric vacua of both IIA and IIB string theory. In particular, we examine the Penrose Inequality, which can be proven holographically using Ryu-Takayanagi, and can be independently proven in SUSY AdS vacua for spherically symmetric initial data. We prove that any EFT of scalars coupled to gravity in AdS, including in particular those of string compactifications, satisfies both the Penrose Inequality and a positive mass theorem if a function that we call a "weak fake superpotential" exists. We demonstrate that this condition is satisfied globally for the DGKT skew-whiffed vacua in IIA. Since there is no known nonperturbative instability in this DGKT vacuum, this provides evidence that the IIA SUSY-broken AdS vacua may be absolutely stable. We also find the weak fake superpotential exists locally in field space in some SUSY-broken AdS vacua in a KKLT construction in IIB. Thus, within the framework considered here, some false SUSY-broken KKLT AdS vacua are stable against vacuum decay. Conversely, we find that some KKLT vacua do not have a weak fake superpotential, and correspondingly violate the Penrose Inequality and fail to have a positive mass theorem; the DGKT vacua only violate the Penrose Inequality in the presence of designer gravity boundary conditions. In all cases studied, this is due to false vacuum decay. We discuss the implications of these violations for holography and black hole thermodynamics in these SUSY-broken AdS vacua.

papers.title: Penalty-Free Constrained Optimization on Dynamic Quantum Circuits via Phase-Protected Tunneling and Closed-Loop Spectral Ratchets
papers.abstract: Embedding hard operational constraints into an unconstrained Hamiltonian via large penalty multipliers induces quadratic spectral aliasing during phase estimation and increases two-qubit gate depth. This paper proposes a penalty-free, closed-loop dynamic quantum circuit scheme, designated as Zeno-decoupled gauge-ratchet optimization (Z-GRO), for constrained binary optimization without outer-loop training. Reversible feasibility phase operators within symmetric dynamical-decoupling echoes confine evolution to the feasible subspace, while an interaction-correlated commutator gauge operator resolves initial symmetry stall. Directional cooling couples the unpenalized objective Hamiltonian to a reusable ancilla with a zero-two-qubit-gate threshold offset, bypassing echoed tunneling gates on retained branches. A survival-filtered Ramsey controller advances the threshold from a linear-programming bound with automatic overshoot rollback. Exact density-matrix and trajectory simulations on spin-glass and quadratic knapsack ensembles show a single-check discrimination gain above four orders of magnitude, improving ground-state probability by factors of 3.0 to 4.3 over quantum Zeno dynamics and 11.4 to 22.5 over penalized schemes. Z-GRO reduces the spin-glass time-to-solution scaling base to 1.529 (compared to 1.684 for quantum Zeno dynamics and 1.909 to 2.047 for penalized schemes) and lowers 14-qubit knapsack time-to-solution by factors of 2.4 to 14.5. For two-qubit gate error rates between $5 \times 10^{-4}$ and $5 \times 10^{-3}$, Z-GRO achieves 2.9 to 7.0 times the optimal probability of noisy penalized feedback, while majority shielding limits loss to 6.3% at a 5.0% readout bit-flip rate, recording 0/24, 0/25, 0/96, 3/25, and 2/80 overshoots.

papers.title: Riemannian Curvature Functionals for de Rham Spectral Triples
papers.abstract: We compute mixed Clifford residue functionals for the Hodge-de Rham operator in even dimensions. A symbol-composition calculation recovers the Riemann and Einstein tensors and yields two ordered curvature functionals with the same classical limit. For specified truncation products on warped collars, we evaluate all five boundary cases and prove that the curvature-recovering antisymmetrizations have no boundary correction. We extend the constructions to spectral data equipped with two one-form actions. Explicit noncommutative torus and finite-direction examples distinguish the functionals and exhibit failures of module balancing and Riemann symmetries. A conformal example shows that a naive exterior lift need not recover classical curvature. The additional structures and limitations of each extension are stated explicitly.

papers.title: Disrupted stars and captured compact objects: Combining observations from multiple messengers to infer the population of massive black holes
papers.abstract: Massive black holes (MBHs) are found in galactic centres, but their formation and evolution remain elusive. Tidal disruption events (TDEs) and extreme mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) both arise from stellar dynamics in the nuclear star clusters around MBHs, and are observed with electromagnetic surveys and gravitational waves, respectively. To overcome the scarcity of coincident detections, we formulate how to combine gravitational-wave detections from LISA-EMRIs with observations from ZTF-TDEs to measure properties of the MBH population. Building on two-dimensional Fokker-Planck simulations of EMRIs and TDEs, we model how their populations are affected by the MBH-host scaling relation, the nucleation fraction and the MBH occupation fraction, and analyse the resulting catalogues using joint hierarchical inference accounting for their individual selection biases. With current ZTF-TDE detections, we can already identify combinations of MBH formation favoured by and consistent with the observed TDE population, and derive corresponding predictions for the EMRI population detectable by LISA. Across a range of astrophysical assumptions, the ratio of detectable TDEs to EMRIs is high: ZTF detecting 2.7-84.3 times as many TDEs as LISA detects EMRIs. TDEs, through their numbers, set the shared mass and redshift distributions: LSST constrains the characteristic MBH mass to a 90% credible width of 0.31 dex and the power-law index of the redshift evolution to a precision of 0.11. EMRIs make up ~3.4% of the joint catalogue, yet carry more information than the whole ZTF sample and are the only probe of MBH spin and orbital eccentricity. TDEs will constrain the abundance of low-mass MBHs before LISA flies, while EMRIs will measure properties that electromagnetic surveys cannot. EMRI and TDE observations offer complementary insights into MBH growth and evolution that neither can provide alone.

papers.title: Single-realization Pauli twirling for suppressing coherent error accumulation in structured quantum circuits
papers.abstract: Pauli twirling is conventionally understood as an ensemble-level noise-tailoring procedure which suppresses coherent components of the error channel by averaging over randomized compilations. This picture does not by itself determine whether a single realization of Pauli-dressed circuit can outperform its bare counterpart, nor does it predict when such an advantage should occur. In this work, we present single-realization based framework for the standard Pauli dressing of two-qubit Clifford gates in structured quantum circuits. This is afforded by the key insight that for weak coherent errors, the leading gate infidelity is governed by the variance of some accumulated error generator. Through both simulations and theoretical considerations, we verify that coherent errors accumulated at different entangling gates can produce $Θ(L^2)$ variance growth in a bare circuit, whereas independent Pauli dressing eliminates the cross-layer contribution on average and yields an $O(L)$ variance bound at any fixed confidence level for a single randomly sampled realization. We then develop a covariance diagnostic that predicts when this mechanism is effective in error mitigation. We find a strong Pauli twirling advantage for coherent errors whose transported generators have large off-diagonal covariance, and little advantage when the covariance matrix is nearly diagonal. Hardware experiments on IBM superconducting processors demonstrate fidelity improvements for GHZ-state preparation and reduced observable errors in Trotterized transverse-field Ising dynamics. These results indicate that single realizations of Pauli twirling without ensemble averaging is a useful coherent-error suppression technique for structured circuits containing repeated nontrivial two-qubit operations.

papers.title: Detection of genuine multipartite entanglement by means of entanglement monotones
papers.abstract: We look for pure state entanglement monotones that may serve as certificates of a strong form of genuine multipartite entanglement, that we refer to as irreducible entanglement: a $D$-partite state (with $D\geq 3$) is irreducibly $D$-partite entangled if it cannot be decomposed as a product of states that are at most $(D-1)$-partite entangled. We start by establishing a no-go result proving that no reasonable genuine multipartite entanglement entropy can simultaneously obey LOCC-monotonicity and subadditivity. After relaxing the first condition to LO-monotonicity, we provide a simple method generating genuine multipartite entanglement monotones with the desired properties. Focusing on a subfamily of these monotones, we show that they are able to detect any form of genuine tripartite entanglement in three-qubit systems.

papers.title: Cosmological Correlators with Triple Massive Exchanges
papers.abstract: Among all tree-level contributions to the primordial bispectrum, the triple exchange of massive scalars is the most challenging. In this paper we present an analytical formula for this bispectrum in the form of a double series, which allows the three exchanged fields to have different masses and converges throughout the whole physical region. We obtain it by expanding the mixed propagator with the softest momentum, so that the triple exchange becomes a sum of integrals over two mixed propagators. Each of these integrals satisfies a differential equation and is fixed by its value at equal momentum. We further show that the squeezed limit follows directly from this formula and takes a simple and compact form.

papers.title: Effective theory of quantum black holes with Kretschmann scalar
papers.abstract: We investigate the thermodynamics, quasinormal modes (QNMs), and shadows of the effective theory of quantum black holes (BHs) by expanding the physical constants in terms of the Kretschmann scalar. The resulting effective metric can contain two horizons, which is typical for a quantum-corrected Schwarzschild spacetime. The second-order corrected metric only shifts the first-order corrected metric, allowing investigation of IR phenomena from the pure first-order corrected one. From a thermodynamic point of view, the metric leads to a stable cold remnant with zero entropy, compatible with the third law of thermodynamics. In the perturbation regime, we use massless scalar perturbations to extract the effective potential, QNMs, graybody factor, and total absorption cross section. We show that double-horizon BHs have a double light ring in the potential, and for a certain value $Ω/χ^2=0.01,$ the QNMs are similar to the GR case since the horizon is Schwarzschild-like. We also tested the correspondence between the QNMs and the graybody factor, and our results still hold with an error far below $1\%$. Our results also conclude that the higher the frequency, the bigger the cross-section area. For the optical observables, we observe that the opposite sign of $Ω$ leads to distinct behavior of the BH's photon sphere and shadow radius. The Sagittarius A* shadow radius upper bound from the Event Horizon Telescope observation in the $2σ$ and $1σ$ significance set the upper limit of the quantum parameter $Ω$ to $Ω/χ^2 \lesssim 0.3649$ and $Ω/χ^2 \lesssim 0.0105$, respectively.

papers.title: $p$-Harmonic gauge and the regularity of spacetime isometries
papers.abstract: We show every Lorentzian metric of class $C^{k,α}$, where $k\in\mathbf{N}_0$ and $α\in(0,1)$, admits local coordinates of class $C^{k+1,α}$ all of whose coordinate functions are temporal functions that are harmonic with respect to a nonlinear $p$-wave operator, where $p\in(-\infty,1)$. Unlike the classical wave operator, this operator is elliptic on temporal functions. As an application, we show that an isometry between Lorentzian metrics of class $C^{k,α}$ is of class $C^{k+1,α}$.

papers.title: Practical insights into controlling exponential concentration in quantum machine learning
papers.abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) models are often limited by exponential concentration, where quantum observables become insensitive to input variations as system size increases. In this work, we provide a comparative empirical study of this phenomenon across Fidelity Quantum Kernels (FQK), Projected Quantum Kernels (PQK), and Quantum Extreme Learning (QEL), within a unified observable-based framework based on expectation-value variance. We investigate how measurement locality, entanglement, and circuit expressivity shape concentration across different architectures. Global fidelity-based kernels exhibit strong concentration driven by Hilbert space dimensionality, whereas local-observable approaches reduce but do not eliminate this effect. In PQK and QEL, concentration is primarily governed by entanglement and quantum dynamical expressivity, with reservoir depth emerging as a key factor in QEL architectures. We further study bandwidth scaling as a general mechanism for controlling encoding expressivity across all models. Our results indicate that bandwidth scaling effectively reduces concentration in moderate regimes by restricting the effective expressivity of the encoding, though this protective effect diminishes in highly expressive structural settings.

papers.title: Polarized IKKT holography: bulk realization of BPS operators
papers.abstract: We study the holographic imprint of polarization in the lowest BPS multiplet of the IKKT matrix model. On the matrix model side, the deformation requires operator mixing and broken-symmetry Ward identities to organize the surviving operators into an irreducible atypical multiplet of the $F(4)$ superalgebra. In the bulk, we use one-dimensional maximal gauged supergravity to identify the analytic half-BPS background with $F(4)$ symmetry whose boundary behavior matches the IKKT polarization. We solve the linearized bosonic and fermionic equations around this background and its undeformed counterpart exactly, and extract the independent asymptotic data. The supersymmetry transformations of these data reproduce the matrix model multiplets, thus establishing a bulk realization of this BPS operator structure.

papers.title: A local symmetry forces positivity for projectively induced Kahler-Einstein metrics
papers.abstract: We prove that a projectively induced Kahler-Einstein metric has positive Einstein constant as soon as it admits one nonzero local real-holomorphic Killing field. Neither completeness nor a prescribed global group action is assumed. This gives a partial answer, under a local symmetry hypothesis, to the general positivity problem for Kahler-Einstein submanifolds of (finite-dimensional) projective space. The key observation is that, by Calabi rigidity, a local real-holomorphic Killing field is induced by a projective unitary vector field whose tangency propagates along any connected global Kahler immersion, without a simple-connectivity assumption. Applied to Hulin's complete continuation, this produces a global Killing field with a bounded Hamiltonian potential given by the ambient projective moment map. The resulting Laplace equation, the Omori--Yau maximum principle and Yau's Liouville theorem exclude both negative and zero Einstein curvature. We also prove a non-Einstein obstruction under uniformly negative Ricci curvature and obtain compact equivariant continuations.

papers.title: A covariant analysis of massless Dirac fields in LRS spacetimes
papers.abstract: We investigate the massless Dirac field in locally rotationally symmetric (LRS) spacetimes using a covariant spinorial-fluid representation, with the spinor current and spin direction aligned with the LRS frame. When the current has both vorticity and sheet twist, characterized by a constant ratio $λ$, the LRS integrability condition relates evolution and propagation derivatives, reducing the field equations to an ordinary differential system that can be integrated exactly. The integrability of the chiral angle forces the heat flux to vanish and the source to saturate the null energy condition along the two radial null directions. A constant boost in the radial Lorentzian two-plane maps the spinor current to a canonical congruence, which is stationary (LRS~I) for $|λ|>1$ and irrotational and geodesic (LRS~III) for $|λ|<1$. In this frame, the local metric is reconstructed in the Goode--Wainwright--Van den Bergh canonical form. For $|λ|>1$ the energy density is positive, and the metric is locally isometric to the horizonless charged Taub--NUT (Brill) metric: in the polar representation, the massless Dirac field supplies a stress--energy tensor algebraically identical to that of the Brill electromagnetic field, with no Maxwell field present. For $|λ|<1$, the energy density is negative and the metric is the hyperbolic ($k=-1$) charged NUT metric with a formal negative squared-charge parameter, whose homogeneous slices are of LRS Bianchi type~VIII.

papers.title: Features investigated: A detailed study of axion monodromy inflation using CLiENT
papers.abstract: We investigate features in the primordial power spectrum from inflation, specifically those predicted by the axion monodromy model, using recent observational data. In order to compute posteriors, profile likelihoods and Bayesian evidence accurately for the complex likelihood surfaces arising in this model we have used the CLiENT emulator framework. As our data combinations we use both a "conservative" set consisting of Planck PR4 temperature, polarisation and lensing data together with DESI DR2 BAO and Pantheon+ supernovae, and a more "aggressive" set which also includes small-scale CMB data from ACT and SPT. We find no robust oscillatory feature in current data. With the conservative data the best fit lies at a frequency $ω\simeq 51$ and lowers $χ^2$ by 10.1 relative to a featureless spectrum. However, this feature is disfavoured by the more aggressive data combination, whose best fit lies at $ω\simeq 31$ and lowers $χ^2$ by 7.4. Fits to featureless data are known to give similar improvements, and the Akaike information criterion, the Bayes factors and the look-elsewhere effect all indicate that neither improvement is significant. The amplitude is limited to $A_\mathrm{osc} < 0.056$ and $A_\mathrm{osc} < 0.062$ (95%) for the two datasets. The emulators reproduce the true log-likelihood at samples of their posteriors with rms errors of 0.07 and 0.16, and the profile likelihoods are calculated with the true likelihood, using the profile capability of CLiENT.

papers.title: Baryon-Enhanced Strong Lensing Signatures of Self-Interacting Dark Matter Subhalos
papers.abstract: Self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) is generally expected to suppress subhalo strong lensing through core formation, with subsequent gravothermal collapse potentially enhancing it. We show that compact stars can make a viable population of galaxy-hosting SIDM subhalos more efficient lenses than their cold dark matter (CDM) counterparts. When the baryonic potential weakens or reverses the inner velocity-dispersion gradient, SIDM halos suppress or bypass core formation, allowing inner densities to grow from early times. The evolved SIDM subhalos produce larger deflection angles and tangential caustics than in CDM. Such galaxy-hosting subhalos also dominate the galaxy-galaxy strong-lensing (GGSL) budget in clusters, yet lie far below the resolution of cosmological simulations. We calibrate a baryonic parametric SIDM model to predict their effects in the three most massive TNG300-1 clusters, finding GGSL cross sections 1.4--2.7 times those in CDM, comparable to the excess inferred in recent analyses. Baryon-enhanced SIDM lensing can thus account for the observed GGSL excess and predicts stronger perturbations from luminous satellites, testable through resolved distortions of background arcs and rings.
